edges.description: Separating DSP from DPP shows that neither is needed to start mineralisation but both are needed for the circumpulpal compartment.
edges.limitations: A true null is not the human genotype. Human disease is caused by heterozygous dominant-negative alleles, and heterozygous Dspp knockout mice have little or no dentine phenotype, so this model informs DSPP function rather than the mechanism of the human dominant disease.

evidence.reference_title: Rough endoplasmic reticulum trafficking errors by different classes of mutant dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP) cause dominant negative effects in both dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia by entrapping normal DSPP.
evidence.snippet: All of this second class of mutations caused mutant DSPP to be retained in the rough endoplasmic reticulum (rER) of transfected HEK293 cells.

nodes.description: Reduced delivery of DSPP to predentine means less of its proteolytic products, dentin sialoprotein and dentin phosphoprotein, at the mineralisation front. Mouse models separating the two show that they are dispensable for the initiation of mineralisation but required for maturation of the circumpulpal dentine, which is the compartment that fails here. The resulting dentine is hypomineralised, with few, large and irregularly oriented tubules and atubular areas.

nodes.description: The enamel is intrinsically normal but the enamel-dentine junction is altered, so enamel shears away along the striae of Retzius, exposing the soft hypomineralised dentine beneath. The exposed dentine often has a hard glassy appearance from sclerosis, and patients rarely complain of sensitivity despite the exposure. What follows from the exposure - attrition - is its own phenotype rather than part of this node.
nodes.id: Enamel Shearing at the Altered Enamel-Dentine Junction

evidence.reference_title: Isolated dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia: revision of the classification.
evidence.snippet: Enamel is often dislodged because of altered enamel dentin junction.

nodes.description: The retained mutant protein forms complexes with co-expressed wild-type DSPP and holds it in the rough endoplasmic reticulum, so secretion of the normal product falls in a dose-dependent way. This is the dominant-negative step, and it also explains the severity gradient between grades: a frameshift allele that retains more of the acidic repeat domain suppresses wild-type secretion more than one that retains none.

evidence.reference_title: Rough endoplasmic reticulum trafficking errors by different classes of mutant dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP) cause dominant negative effects in both dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia by entrapping normal DSPP.
evidence.snippet: Trafficking out of the rER by coexpressed normal DSPP was reduced in a dose-responsive manner, probably due to formation of Ca2+-dependent complexes with the retained mutant DSPP.

nodes.description: Rapid wear of exposed dentine once enamel has sheared off, ranging from a few erosion facets to complete disappearance of the crown, and often requiring overdenture management in the primary dentition.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia: revision of the classification.
evidence.snippet: Attrition ranges from few facets of erosion to a complete disappearance of the crown.

nodes.description: Management is restorative and preventive: early diagnosis followed by full-coverage protection of affected teeth to arrest attrition, preserve occlusal vertical dimension and maintain aesthetics, with overdentures often used in the primary dentition. There is no treatment directed at the underlying dentine defect.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary dentine disorders: dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentine dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: In the primary dentition, stainless steel crowns on the molars may be used to prevent tooth wear and maintain the occlusal vertical dimension.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary dentine disorders: dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentine dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: Cast occlusal onlays on the first permanent molars and eventually the premolars, help to minimise tooth wear and maintain the occlusal vertical dimension

nodes.description: A single germline DSPP allele initiates disease. Two mutation classes dominate: 5-prime changes affecting the signal peptide, the signal-peptidase cleavage site or the IPV motif at the start of the mature protein (exons 2-3), and 3-prime single-base indels in the long repetitive exon 5 encoding dentin phosphoprotein, which shift translation into the -1 reading frame. The pattern itself is informative: true nonsense alleles are not reported, and heterozygous Dspp knockout mice have little or no dentine phenotype, so simple loss of function does not produce the dominant human disease.

evidence.reference_title: Mouse Dspp frameshift model of human dentinogenesis imperfecta.
evidence.snippet: The pattern of mutations strongly supports the conclusion that simple loss-of-function mutations do not cause dominant dentin malformations in humans

evidence.reference_title: Rough endoplasmic reticulum trafficking errors by different classes of mutant dentin sialophosphoprotein (DSPP) cause dominant negative effects in both dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia by entrapping normal DSPP.
evidence.snippet: loss of a single allele is recessive and that haploinsufficiency does not explain DD or DGI

genetic_context.description: Germline heterozygous DSPP variant acting through a dominant-negative mechanism rather than haploinsufficiency.

nodes.description: Mutant DSPP fails to exit the rough endoplasmic reticulum. For 5-prime variants the block is after signal-peptide processing: mutant protein stays endoglycosidase H-sensitive and co-localises with an rER marker while wild-type reaches Golgi-like puncta. For 3-prime frameshift alleles the -1 frame appends a long hydrophobic C-terminal extension that is thought to anchor the protein in the rER membrane. Splicing is unaffected.

nodes.description: Both dentitions show grey-blue to amber-brown opalescent discolouration, present from eruption. Primary teeth are often more severely affected than permanent teeth, which inverts the usual expectation and matters for counselling and for the timing of definitive restorative work.

nodes.description: Where a child presents late and the teeth have already worn to the level of the gingivae, overdentures are the remaining option; children adapt well but the dentures must be remade as they grow. Dental implants are considered once growth is complete at about 18 years, and ridge augmentation is often needed first because early tooth loss leaves maxillo-mandibular atrophy. This row is the counterpart of the restorative one: it is what is left when protection came too late.
nodes.id: Overdentures and implant-retained prosthetics for late or advanced presentation

evidence.snippet: If, however the child presents late, the teeth may have undergone attrition to the level of the gingivae and the only treatment option then is to provide over-dentures

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary dentine disorders: dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentine dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: Dental implants may be considered when growth is complete at about 18 years of age.

nodes.description: Teeth are lost early through short or absent roots and spontaneous abscess formation. Prevention and regular dental care do not avert it, which sets the ceiling on what management can achieve.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary dentine disorders: dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentine dysplasia.
evidence.snippet: Early diagnosis and regular dental care however cannot prevent premature tooth-loss due to short or absent roots and spontaneous abscess formation that occurs in some types of DGI and DD

nodes.description: Progressive obliteration of the pulp chamber and root canals by abnormal dentine. At the severe, 5-prime end of the spectrum the opposite is seen - pulp enlargement and hollow "shell teeth" - which is why the grade and the mutation class are recorded together.

evidence.reference_title: Isolated dentinogenesis imperfecta and dentin dysplasia: revision of the classification.
evidence.snippet: The radiographical aspect is pathognomonic: bulbous crowns because of an important cervical constriction, short and thick roots and pulp obliteration.
